remediation_steps.step:
Back up the source file before making any edits.

Command:
    cp /opt/vuln-labs/serverless-lab/lambda_function.py /opt/vuln-labs/serverless-lab/lambda_function.py.bak-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)

Why: Creating a backup ensures that you can restore the original state of the file if the changes introduce any issues.

Replace the vulnerable os.system call with subprocess.run using a list of arguments to safely execute the command.

Command:
    #EDIT_FILE
    {"path": "/opt/vuln-labs/serverless-lab/lambda_function.py",
     "old_text": "os.system(\"cat /tmp/" + filename)",
     "new_text": "subprocess.run(['cat', '/tmp/' + filename], check=True)"}

Why: Using subprocess.run with a list of arguments prevents shell injection by avoiding the shell's interpretation of the command string.

Verify that the vulnerable pattern is no longer present in the file.

Command:
    #VERIFY_ABSENT
    {"path": "/opt/vuln-labs/serverless-lab/lambda_function.py",
     "pattern": "os.system(\"cat /tmp/" + filename)"}

Why: Ensuring the absence of the vulnerable pattern confirms that the fix has been applied correctly.

Perform a syntax check to ensure the file is still valid Python code after the edit.

Command:
    python3 -m py_compile /opt/vuln-labs/serverless-lab/lambda_function.py

Why: Syntax checking ensures that the changes have not introduced any syntax errors into the code.
